posts.title: Form 700, Explained: What It Can't Tell You
posts.caption:
Form 700, Explained: what the form can't tell you.

A Form 700 is California's Statement of Economic Interests - public record, five schedules: A investments and business positions, B real property, C income, D gifts, E travel payments.

This episode teaches the limits. The form reports ranges, not exact dollars. A listed interest is not proof of wrongdoing, and a clean form is not proof of clean conduct. A blank is a signed statement, checkable against property and business records. The form cannot show what was left off it - but amendments are public too, and the original stays on the record.

Worked example: the filing of Rodrigo Espinosa Rios, Merced County Board of Education, Area 4 - farm income over $100,000, parcels in Delhi, and an elected-income line reading Supervisor, District 1. Two lines, one filing. The form does not resolve the gap. It shows you where to look.

Read the filing, then read the votes, the contracts, and the calendar. The record first, always.
